_doc: AI-CHAT-UI policy. The fleet draws its AI chat ONCE: libs:ai (ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ai, package com.diegonmarcos.superapp.ai): the page (conversation, streaming answer, Agent and Model pickers, Sessions, input), the consent card a mutating tool waits on, the assistant panel, the backends (the fleet gateway, OpenRouter) and the shared contract assets/ai/ai.json. Cloud Search, Cloud Browser, Cloud Drive and Cloud Tools Small LLMs host it with their own theme, store and token; Cloud Code (JS) reads the same ai.json. Consumed by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-ai-chat-guard.py, which fails when Kotlin outside the owner draws an AI chat of its own. Nothing in the script names an app, a path or a marker: adding a rule, an exemption or a root is a DATA edit here.
_rule: one AI chat UI in the fleet's Kotlin apps, libs:ai's; an app hosts it, it does not draw its own.
_doc_owner: The one tree allowed to draw the chat. It must also still HOLD the chat (owner_must_hold): a guard whose owner was emptied would stay green for every app that copied the page back out.
_doc_scan_prefixes: A top-level directory starting with any of these is an app, solution or shared-lib tree and is scanned (Kotlin only). Cloud Code's JS chat is not Kotlin: its contract is held by ac_cloud-code/test/test-chat.sh.
_doc_skip_path_parts: Test sources may name the roles and the endpoint to prove a host's behaviour (Cloud Search's SearchShellTest posts to the gateway through a fake). They draw nothing in the app.

exempt.why: Element X, a vendored Matrix messenger: its chat is people talking to people, not an AI chat.
Mattermost, a vendored team messenger: people talking to people, not an AI chat.

role-bubble.why: a composable that branches on the OpenAI message roles is drawing the chat's bubbles

chat-composable._doc_unless_file_contains: A file that CALLS libs:ai's page or panel is the host's wrapper around it (Cloud Search's AssistantPage hands the lib its theme and engines): a name is fine there. The role-bubble rule still applies to it, so a host that also draws bubbles is caught.
chat-composable.why: a composable named as a chat page, screen or panel is a second chat UI

ui-calls-model.why: a composable file that names the model endpoint or the gateway's mode header talks to the model itself, instead of through libs:ai's host
